messages:

Subject: Realtime demo recap — connection strategy & quota asks

Hi Ellen / PayFlux team,

Really appreciate you taking the time yesterday for the live demo. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so everyone has a single place to pick up next week: 

Key takeaways from the demo:
- Streaming use case: long-running sessions (user conversations) with interleaved short completions (notifications).
- Target p95 token latency for streaming: ~120ms once warmed (90–110ms ideal for production).
- Expected average concurrency during peak: 220–320 active streams, with spikes to ~500 for 60–120s during batch events.
- Sustained non-streaming RPS (short prompt/complete calls): ~600 req/s.

Immediate asks (what we need to run a pilot):
1) Redwood to provide a recommended connection strategy (multiplexing per TCP connection, suggested streams-per-conn, and conservative burst settings).
2) A draft rate-limit matrix that maps: connections / streams-per-connection / per-connection token-rate / burst window.
3) Access to a short test harness (we attached a Postman collection and sample requests) so PayFlux can run synthetic traffic against a pilot endpoint.
4) Confirmation of any hard rate caps we should expect in the pilot and a proposed escalation path if the pilot needs temporary burst increases.

Attachments: payflux-concurrency-requirements.xlsx (your sheet), conn-test-harness-postman.json (test collection), redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (proposal).

Ben / Karthik — can you draft a starting rate-limit matrix and suggested streams-per-connection today? I put the high-level constraints in the spreadsheet for reference.

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: Realtime demo recap — connection strategy & quota asks

Thanks Olga — great session. A few clarifications from our engineering side after reviewing the recording and the spreadsheet: 

- Latency: p95 target is 120ms for user-facing chat; we can tolerate 200ms briefly during cold starts. We also need tail guarantees for end-of-conversation flushes (no more than 400ms).
- Concurrency: the 220–320 active streams number is correct for day-to-day; the burst to 500 is likely during promotions. Bursts are short (typically 1–2 minutes).
- Multiplexing: We are open to 4–12 logical streams per TCP/WebSocket, but our infra team prefers fewer streams-per-conn to simplify proxies.
- Throughput: non-streaming ~600 rps sustained, with occasional spikes to 1.2k rps for 30–90s.

Question: What would Redwood recommend for a pilot that limits complexity while giving us a realistic stress signal? For example, start with 8 streams/conn and 250 parallel connections vs. a smaller footprint?

We'll run the attached Postman harness early next week once you provide an endpoint and a candidate rate matrix to validate. Also incl. our billing and security contacts in a following thread.

Cheers,
Ellen

Ellen Park
Head of Platform Engineering | PayFlux
ellen@payflux.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Realtime demo recap — connection strategy & quota asks

Ellen — thanks for the details. Proposed pilot configuration below (we tried to balance conservative defaults with what will exercise your burst profile):

Pilot proposal (14-day):
- Endpoint: dedicated pilot API (private URL) with token-based auth.
- Connections: allow up to 300 concurrent TCP/WebSocket connections (soft limit for pilot).
- Streams per connection: default 6 logical streams per connection; allow up to 10 when proxies permit.
- Stream-level token-rate: 25 tokens/sec nominal, burst to 200 tokens over a 2s window (this prevents single-stream hogging).
- Connection-level token throughput: up to 1,500 tokens/sec nominal (based on 6 streams * 25 t/s) with burst gating aligned to stream bursts.
- Non-streaming RPS: rate limit at 1,200 rps sustained, with 2k rps brief burst token.
- Backpressure policy: 429 with Retry-After when connection-level token budget exhausted; soft 503 fallback to a smaller model variant for graceful degradation.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching: enable conversational prefix caching to reduce token load for repeated system prompts.
- Observability: we'll surface per-connection token consumption, stream occupancy, and p95/p99 latency.
- Escalation: temporary burst increases (+20–50% caps) require a 1-hr SLA window to approve; we're fine to fast-track during pilot test windows.

Attached: a one-page rate matrix and the redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf. If this looks good, Karthik will spin up the pilot endpoint and we’ll share credentials. We recommend you start with 6 streams/conn and a 300-conn soft cap; that should reproduce your spike behavior without running into global hard limits.

Ben

2) Provision the soft caps Ben suggested (300 connections / 6 streams per conn default / 25 tps per stream) and instrument per-connection metrics in the console.
3) Share a short runbook for the test harness (how to ramp and what to inspect).
4) We'll also attach a small benchmark script (curl + jq) you can use if Postman misses concurrency edges.

Please confirm an initial 2-hour test window Thursday 09:00–11:00 PT when PayFlux will generate the spike profile. If that works, we'll enable the temporary burst window and observe metrics together.
